explanation: Fires on a word or word-piece in the middle of a fixed multi-token name, term or formula, where the next token is highly predictable: named entities and proper-name compounds (Clauser-Horne, Banana River, Woods Hole Oceanographic, Savannah River, Hind III), technical collocations (cesarean section, crystal oscillator, private key, work in progress, +/-), and repeated templates in synthetic math problems (' Solve', ' Suppose', 'greatest common factor of'). Ordinary prose tokens with no fixed continuation give weak or no activation.

Fires mainly on a word-initial 'K'/'k' token that starts a foreign or unusual word or name (Kiso, kring, kudos, KGB, Kobe, Konnichi, Kaffee, Konto, Künstler, Kamchatka). A weaker, separate response appears on CJK characters in Chinese/Japanese text and on other capitalized foreign name pieces (Oh, Bel, Pok, G).

Fires on separators and connectors inside structured or formulaic text: range and score separators between numbers ('18-39', '47-37', '7–5', '2.5 to 3.5', '3:00-4:00'), path and URL slashes, and boilerplate or layout tokens in legal captions, license headers, counsel listings and code. Range dashes between numbers are the most reliable trigger; ordinary prose words fire weakly.

Fires only on a '0' token inside a long run of zeros (e.g. '000000000 +080'), at full strength. Every other context gives about 1% or less, so it is effectively a detector for long runs of zero digits.

Fires weakly on a diffuse set of tokens that continue a phrase, such as the second word of fixed expressions ('made up', 'most of all', 'calls another'), thousands-separator commas inside numbers (81,000), license-header words ('this work', ' *'), and repeated items in sequences. There is no clear unifying feature, and the strongest example is a single Q&A snippet.

A mixture: completions of word-pieces inside proper names and terms (tableaux, Bolivarian, LSTM, Intelligenz, Pepperdine, HOLIDAY), the 'h' in the template 'k'th term', 'you' in 'brought to you' or 'inform you', and line breaks in legal document captions. No single feature predicts activation.

Fires on function and connective words inside standard software license and copyright boilerplate, above all 'even' in 'WITHOUT ANY WARRANTY; without even the implied warranty', and also 'except' in 'use this file except in compliance', 'that' in 'provided that the following conditions', and 'part' in 'This file is part of'. Outside license text it fires only weakly and sporadically.

Fires on the token that opens a new clause or sentence in emotive or argumentative prose: the word right after a period, semicolon or colon ('Frustration[.]', ';[ the] pain', '[It] wasn't', ' With'), or a subject or modal starting a new clause ('You can', 'I've', 'He thinks'). Context matters more than the token itself, and neutral or technical text fires weakly.

Fires on function words and conjunctions that join clauses, especially in German (dass, zu, hat, war, so dass), and on 'Unless' at the start of the Apache license line 'Unless required by applicable law'. It also responds to quantifier and preposition words in English idioms ('size of', 'most of', 'one or both', 'unless otherwise'). Content words fire weakly.

Fires on the start or middle of a multi-piece word, at a subword that begins a longer word (INS-urance, ret-roject, irrev-ocable, Rep-roduction, norm-otensive, zip-ras-idone, Osch-ersleben), across languages and domains, plus a few unrelated cases ('West' in 'West Bank', 'not' in a disclaimer). It is driven by word-piece position, not meaning.

A mixture: CJK characters in Chinese strings, commas between place names ('Taichung, Taiwan', 'New South Wales, South Australia'), code tokens after operators or quotes, citation numbers, and articles such as 'a' or 'the' in set phrases. No coherent single trigger.
Fires only on a '0' token inside a long run of zeros (e.g. '0000000 +020', '000000000 0531'). Everything else is about 1% or less, so it is effectively a long-zero-run detector.

Fires on a wide variety of tokens with no shared meaning: closing parentheses and brackets in code, 'to' in 'as to', 'all' in 'in all copies', math operators in equations, suffixes of long words (-ibility, -udes), and Japanese or Turkish morphemes. Tokens that end a phrase or complete a fixed expression may be favored, but this is weakly supported.

Fires at full strength only on a '0' token inside a long run of zeros. All other contexts fire at about 12% or less, with faint responses to rare word-pieces (yc, ach, NOTICE). It is essentially a long-zero-run detector.
